## Anomaly
{"kind": "fun", "system": "replicatedstorage/gameassets.luau", "severity": "medium", "title": "[ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets.luau] Lighting is set up (atmosphere, bloom, colour correction), but the scene has particles=0, beams=0 and highlights=0, so there is no ambient sparkle. Bloom threshold 1.6 is high, so Neon parts barely glow. The world feels static.", "expected": "Lower bloom.Threshold to about 1.0 and raise Intensity to 0.8 so Neon pads and gates visibly glow. Make the GameAssets burst helper create and Emit real ParticleEmitters (sparkle texture, gold and theme colours, 20 particles) for purchases and rebirth, and export a helper that attaches a slow ambient sparkle emitter to the plaza fountain.", "observed": "Lighting is set up (atmosphere, bloom, colour correction), but the scene has particles=0, beams=0 and highlights=0, so there is no ambient sparkle. Bloom threshold 1.6 is high, so Neon parts barely glow. The world feels static.", "path": "ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets.luau"}

## Investigation
Conclusion: {"root_cause": "The plaza fountain never gets an ambient sparkle emitter. The bloom is already correct at runtime (Threshold 1, Intensity 0.8), and GameAssets.burst and GameAssets.ambient both create real ParticleEmitters. The gap is that nothing attaches ambient sparkle to the fountain. GameAssets.sparkleFountain only works if it can find an object named 'Fountain'. PlazaBuilder.buildPlaza builds the fountain as loose parts (Basin, Water, Column, Bowl, Spout) in the Plaza folder and none is named Fountain. No caller attaches ambient sparkle at runtime either: 0 AmbientSparkleAttachment instances exist, and calling sparkleFountain on the live plaza adds none. So the scene has only the 7 emitters (6 collector emitters at rate 0, plus the rebirth altar), 0 beams and 0 highlights, and the world feels static.", "file": "ServerScriptService/PlazaBuilder.luau", "evidence": "Probe 2: Bloom Threshold=1, Intensity=0.8, ambient attachments=0, beams=0, highlights=0, emitters=7. Probe 5: sparkleFountain returns without error but the attachment count stays 0 (before=0, after=0). Probe 6: no object has 'fountain' in its name, yet GameAssets.ambient(workspace.Plaza.Spout) works and returns an emitter at rate 8. Probe 7: with a temporary Model named 'Fountain', sparkleFountain does attach AmbientSparkleAttachment to it.", "fix_hint": "At the end of PlazaBuilder.buildPlaza, after f.Parent = Workspace, require ReplicatedStorage.GameAssets and call GameAssets.ambient(spout, nil, 8) on the Spout

Probe (Server): Call sparkleFountain manually to see if it works and whether anything had already called it (before=0 means no caller at runtime)
```luau
local ga=require(game.ReplicatedStorage.GameAssets)
local before=0
for _,d in workspace:GetDescendants() do if d.Name=="AmbientSparkleAttachment" then before+=1 end end
local ok,res=pcall(ga.sparkleFountain)
local after=0
for _,d in workspace:GetDescendants() do if d.Name=="AmbientSparkleAttachment" then after+=1 end end
return tostring(ok).." "..tostring(res).." before="..before.." after="..after
```
Result: true nil before=0 after=0

Probe (Server): Verify ambient works on the Spout and see why sparkleFountain finds no target (no object named fountain)
```luau
local ga=require(game.ReplicatedStorage.GameAssets)
local sp=workspace.Plaza.Spout
local e=ga.ambient(sp)
local names={}
for _,d in workspace:GetDescendants() do local n=d.Name:lower() if n:find("fountain") then table.insert(names,d:GetFullName()) end end
local ok,res=pcall(ga.sparkleFountain)
return tostring(e)..' rate='..tostring(e and e.Rate)..' fountainNamed='..table.concat(names,',')..' sf='..tostring(res)
```
Result: AmbientSparkle rate=8 fountainNamed= sf=nil

Probe (Server): Control: does sparkleFountain work when an object named Fountain exists?
```luau
local ga=require(game.ReplicatedStorage.GameAssets)
local m=Instance.new("Model") m.Name="Fountain"
local p=Instance.new("Part") p.Anchored=true p.Size=Vector3.new(4,2,4) p.Position=Vector3.new(0,50,0) p.Parent=m
m.PrimaryPart=p
m.Parent=workspace
pcall(ga.sparkleFountain)
local found=0
for _,d in workspace:GetDescendants() do if d.Name=="AmbientSparkleAttachment" then found+=1 end end
local inFountain = p:FindFirstChild("AmbientSparkleAttachment")~=nil
m:Destroy()
return "found="..found.." inFountain="..tostring(inFountain)
```
Result: found=2 inFountain=true

## Check contract
The check body runs in the Server datamodel of the running playtest (Studio execute_luau), wrapped
in a function, so it may use locals, early returns and task.wait (stay under 20 seconds in total).
It must return { ok = boolean, detail = string }. ok = true means the game behaves correctly.
A Luau error or a missing return counts as a failed run, but it does NOT prove the bug: only a clean
ok = false does. The playtest has the Studio player (Players:GetPlayers()[1]) once they have joined.
Live server modules can be reached with require(<ModuleScript>) or
game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevHook:Invoke(moduleName, method, ...).
Undo what the check sets up (cash, positions, spawned parts) before every return.
ok = false must mean "the game did the wrong thing". When the check cannot set up its situation (no player,
no plot, a part or module missing), call error("setup: <what is missing>") instead: that is a broken check,
not a proven bug, and an ok = false for it makes every fix look like a failure.
"Correct" is what the anomaly and the game's spec expect. Never redefine it just to get a failing check.
The third header line names the consumer: `-- consumer: <file>:<line>`, the game code (client or server)
that reads or uses what the check asserts, from the line-numbered code below. A check whose premise no game
code depends on proves nothing, and Forge will not count it.

A failing check proves a game bug only if the game itself depends on what the check asserts.
Name the consumer: the game code path (client or server) that reads or uses the asserted thing, as
<file>:<line> from the line-numbered code shown. A config value or the code that creates the thing is not a
consumer. If no game code reads it (the check expects an object in a place nothing looks, a name nothing
uses), the check's premise is wrong: it is a check bug, not a game bug.

## Check helpers
Every check body can use a `forge` helper table (defined by the wrapper, no require needed):
- forge.waitFor(fn, timeout) -> the first truthy value fn() returns within timeout seconds (default 10), else nil.
- forge.startRound(timeout) -> starts a round through the ForgeTest harness (no-op if workspace RoundState is
  already "Active") and waits until RoundState is "Active"; raises "setup: ..." when it cannot.
- forge.endRound() -> ends the round (call it before returning when the check started one).
A check never waits for a lobby countdown or a player to pick a mission: it calls forge.startRound().

## Example checks
```luau
-- check: Touching an affordable buy pad takes its price and marks it bought
-- covers: anomaly: buy pads never unlock
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
local t0 = os.clock()
while not (p and p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) and os.clock() - t0 < 10 do
	task.wait(0.5)
	p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
end
if not p or not p.Character then error("setup: no player character within 10s") end
local cash = p.leaderstats.Cash
local pad = workspace:FindFirstChild("BuyPad_dropper2", true)
if not pad then error("setup: no BuyPad_dropper2 in workspace") end
local hrp = p.Character.HumanoidRootPart
local oldCash, oldCF = cash.Value, hrp.CFrame
cash.Value = 1000
hrp.CFrame = pad.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
local t1 = os.clock()
while cash.Value == 1000 and os.clock() - t1 < 3 do task.wait(0.1) end
local spent = 1000 - cash.Value
cash.Value, hrp.CFrame = oldCash, oldCF
return { ok = spent == 25, detail = "pad took " .. spent .. " cash, expected 25" }
```
